extra_vocab.en: a person who makes a phone call
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於客服、櫃檯與電話留言情境，例如詢問來電者姓名、請來電者留言或轉接分機。

example.en: Several callers complained about the long wait on the phone line.
example.zh: 好幾位來電者抱怨電話等候太久。

example.en: The caller ID showed a number from our London office.
example.zh: 來電顯示是我們倫敦辦公室的號碼。

example.en: Do not give company information to an unknown caller.
example.zh: 不要把公司資訊透露給不明來電者。

example.en: He is a regular caller who orders supplies every month.
example.zh: 他是常客，每個月都打電話訂貨。

examples.en: The caller asked to speak with someone in the billing department.
examples.zh: 來電者要求和帳務部門的人通話。

examples.en: Please ask the caller to leave a name and number.
examples.zh: 請請來電者留下姓名和電話。

examples.en: Our receptionist greets every caller in a friendly voice.
examples.zh: 我們的櫃檯人員用親切的聲音招呼每位來電者。

confusable.diff: collar 是「衣領」，發音與拼法和 caller 很像，但和電話無關。

example.en: The new uniform has a white collar and a red tie.
example.zh: 新制服有白色衣領和紅色領帶。

example.en: The operator connected me to the sales manager at once.
example.zh: 總機馬上把我轉接給業務經理。

example.en: The receptionist will take your message and pass it on.
example.zh: 櫃檯人員會記下你的留言並轉達。

example.en: Please leave a voicemail if I do not answer.
example.zh: 如果我沒接電話，請留語音訊息。

example.en: Please dial extension 305 to reach the accounting team.
example.zh: 請撥分機 305 找會計團隊。

derived.link: 最基礎的字。caller = call + -er，打電話的人，像 teacher、worker

extra_vocab.zh: 休閒的、隨意的、非正式的
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於服裝規定（casual dress）、非正式的談話與聚會，也可指臨時性的工作。

example.en: Casual dress is welcome at the company picnic on Saturday.
example.zh: 星期六的公司野餐歡迎穿休閒服裝。

example.en: We had a casual conversation about the project over coffee.
example.zh: 我們喝咖啡時輕鬆聊了一下這個專案。

example.en: Our office has a casual Friday policy all year round.
example.zh: 我們辦公室全年都有週五便服日的規定。

examples.en: Employees may wear casual clothes every Friday this summer.
examples.zh: 今年夏天，員工每個星期五可以穿便服。

examples.en: The manager gave a casual talk instead of a long speech.
examples.zh: 經理做了一場輕鬆的談話，而不是冗長的演講。

examples.en: We hire casual workers during the busy holiday season.
examples.zh: 我們在忙碌的假期旺季僱用臨時工。

confusable.diff: causal 是「因果的」，只差一個字母，常和 casual 看錯。

example.en: The study shows a causal link between sleep and work results.
example.zh: 這項研究顯示睡眠與工作成果之間有因果關係。

similar.diff: informal 強調不是正式的場合或用語；casual 還有輕鬆隨意的感覺。

example.en: The party will be informal, so you do not need a suit.
example.zh: 這場聚會很隨性，所以你不需要穿西裝。

similar.diff: relaxed 強調氣氛放鬆、不緊張；casual 常用於服裝與態度。

example.en: The team meeting had a relaxed atmosphere this morning.
example.zh: 今天早上的團隊會議氣氛很輕鬆。

example.en: A formal letter should end with a polite closing.
example.zh: 正式的信件應該以禮貌的結語收尾。

example.en: The dress code for the dinner is formal.
example.zh: 這場晚宴的服裝規定是正式服裝。

example.en: These shoes are comfortable enough to wear all day.
example.zh: 這雙鞋舒服到可以穿一整天。

example.en: Staff must wear a uniform while they are on duty.
example.zh: 員工值班時必須穿制服。

derived.link: casual + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quick → quickly

example.en: She wore a casual jacket to the client lunch.
example.zh: 她穿休閒外套去赴客戶午餐。

senses.en: done without much thought or planning
senses.distinguish: 後面接 comment、remark 這類字時，指隨口說說、不是認真的。

example.en: It was only a casual comment, so please do not worry.
example.zh: 那只是隨口說說的評論，所以請不用擔心。

senses.en: not working all the time or for a long period
senses.distinguish: 後面接 job、worker、labor 時，指不是正式、長期的工作。

example.en: He took a casual job at the warehouse last summer.
example.zh: 他去年夏天在倉庫做了一份臨時工作。

extra_vocab.en: the person who leads a meeting or a group
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於會議、董事會與委員會情境，不分性別，是 chairman 的中性說法。

example.en: The chairpersons of both committees will meet on Thursday.
example.zh: 兩個委員會的主席星期四會面。

example.en: The board will elect a new chairperson next month.
example.zh: 董事會下個月會選出新主席。

example.en: She has served as chairperson for three years.
example.zh: 她已經擔任主席三年了。

example.en: We need to appoint a chairperson before the vote begins.
example.zh: 我們需要在投票開始前任命一位主席。

example.en: The chairperson of the committee opened the meeting at nine.
example.zh: 委員會主席九點開始這場會議。

examples.en: The chairperson asked everyone to turn off their phones.
examples.zh: 主席請大家把手機關掉。

examples.en: Our chairperson will give the opening speech tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 我們的主席明天早上會致開幕詞。

examples.en: The chairperson thanked all members for their hard work this year.
examples.zh: 主席感謝所有成員今年的辛勞。

confusable.diff: 意思相同，但 chairman 字面上指男性；現在較常用中性的 chairperson 或 chair。

example.en: The chairman of the board announced the new plan.
example.zh: 董事長宣布了新計畫。

similar.diff: chair 也可指「主席」，口語更簡短；它還是動詞，表示「主持（會議）」。

example.en: Mr. Kim will chair the meeting this afternoon.
example.zh: 金先生今天下午會主持會議。

example.en: The committee meets on the first Monday of every month.
example.zh: 委員會每個月第一個星期一開會。

example.en: The board approved the budget at yesterday's meeting.
example.zh: 董事會在昨天的會議上通過了預算。

example.en: Please read the agenda before the meeting starts.
example.zh: 請在會議開始前閱讀議程。

example.en: The director will explain the new rules to everyone.
example.zh: 主管會向大家說明新規定。

derived.link: 最基礎的字。chairperson = chair（主席）+ person（人）
chair + man，指男性主席，像 salesman
chair + woman，指女性主席，和 chairman 相對

extra_vocab.en: to shout to show support or happiness
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於活動、運動比賽與慶祝情境；cheer up 表示讓人心情變好，名詞 cheer 指歡呼聲。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: cheer up 可以拆開，受詞是代名詞時要放中間：cheer him up，不說 cheer up him。為某人加油用 cheer for 或 cheer on。

example.en: The crowd cheers whenever our team scores a point.
example.zh: 每當我們的隊伍得分，群眾就歡呼。

example.en: Loud cheers filled the hall when the winner was announced.
example.zh: 宣布得獎者時，歡呼聲充滿了大廳。

example.en: Staff cheered when the manager announced the bonus plan.
example.zh: 經理宣布獎金計畫時，員工們歡呼起來。

example.en: The fans are cheering outside the stadium right now.
example.zh: 球迷們現在正在體育場外歡呼。

example.en: Employees came to cheer for the company's soccer team.
example.zh: 員工們來為公司的足球隊加油。

example.en: A short break can cheer up a tired team.
example.zh: 短暫的休息可以讓疲累的團隊重新振作。

example.en: Customers gathered to cheer on the marathon runners.
example.zh: 顧客們聚集起來為馬拉松跑者加油打氣。

example.en: The audience gave a cheer at the end of the speech.
example.zh: 演講結束時，觀眾歡呼了一聲。

examples.en: The crowd began to cheer when the CEO walked on stage.
examples.zh: 執行長走上舞台時，群眾開始歡呼。

examples.en: Everyone cheered after the team won the sales contest.
examples.zh: 團隊贏得業績競賽後，大家都歡呼起來。

examples.en: Thousands of fans cheer for their teams at the stadium.
examples.zh: 數千名球迷在體育場為他們的球隊加油。

confusable.diff: chair 是「椅子、主席」，發音接近 cheer，聽力時容易搞混。

example.en: Please take a chair near the stage and wait for the show.
example.zh: 請在舞台附近找張椅子坐下，等候表演。

similar.diff: applaud 是拍手鼓掌，語氣較正式；cheer 是大聲歡呼。

example.en: The audience stood up to applaud the speaker.
example.zh: 觀眾起立為講者鼓掌。

example.en: We will celebrate our tenth anniversary with a party.
example.zh: 我們會舉辦派對慶祝十週年。

example.en: Managers should encourage staff to share new ideas.
example.zh: 主管應該鼓勵員工分享新點子。

example.en: Thank you for your support during the busy season.
example.zh: 謝謝你在忙季時的支持。

example.en: A large crowd waited outside the store before opening.
example.zh: 開店前，一大群人在店外等候。

derived.link: cheer + -ful（充滿），充滿歡樂的，像 helpful、useful
cheerful + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 helpful → helpfully

example.en: Visitors cheer loudly at the end of each performance.
example.zh: 每場表演結束時，遊客都大聲歡呼。

example.en: A cheer rose from the crowd as the show began.
example.zh: 表演開始時，群眾中響起一陣歡呼。

senses.en: to shout loudly to show support or joy

example.en: The workers cheered as the new factory opened.
example.zh: 新工廠開幕時，工人們歡呼起來。

senses.distinguish: 後面接 up 且受詞是人時，是安慰、使振作，不是大聲歡呼。

example.en: The good news cheered everyone up after a hard week.
example.zh: 好消息讓大家在辛苦的一週後重新打起精神。

extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於天氣、辦公室溫度與戶外活動情境；也可形容態度冷淡，例如 a chilly reception。

example.en: The office feels chillier in the morning than in the afternoon.
example.zh: 辦公室早上比下午感覺更冷。

example.en: Yesterday was the chilliest day of the whole week.
example.zh: 昨天是整個星期最冷的一天。

example.en: Chilly weather may lower sales at our outdoor cafe.
example.zh: 寒冷的天氣可能會降低我們戶外咖啡廳的銷售。

example.en: It was a chilly morning, so we wore thick coats.
example.zh: 那是個涼颼颼的早晨，所以我們穿了厚外套。

collocations.zh: 冷淡的接待、冷淡的反應

example.en: The new plan received a chilly reception from the staff.
example.zh: 新計畫得到員工冷淡的反應。

example.en: I feel chilly, so please turn off the air conditioner.
example.zh: 我覺得冷，所以請關掉冷氣。

examples.en: The meeting room is too chilly, so please close the window.
examples.zh: 會議室太冷了，所以請關上窗戶。

examples.en: It gets chilly in the evening, so bring a jacket.
examples.zh: 晚上會變涼，所以請帶一件外套。

examples.en: The hotel lobby was chilly after we arrived from the airport.
examples.zh: 我們從機場抵達後，飯店大廳感覺涼颼颼的。

confusable.diff: chili 是「辣椒」，發音和 chilly 一樣，但意思是食物，不是天氣。

example.en: The restaurant serves a spicy chili soup on cold days.
example.zh: 這間餐廳在寒冷的日子供應辛辣的辣椒湯。

similar.diff: cold 是一般的冷，程度可能更強；chilly 是有點冷、感到不舒服。

example.en: It is very cold outside, so wear a warm coat.
example.zh: 外面很冷，所以請穿暖和的外套。

similar.diff: cool 是涼爽、通常讓人舒服；chilly 比較冷，讓人想多穿衣服。

example.en: The cool air in the lobby felt nice after the walk.
example.zh: 走了一段路後，大廳的涼風感覺很舒服。

example.en: The room temperature is set to twenty-two degrees.
example.zh: 室內溫度設定為二十二度。

example.en: Please bring a jacket for the outdoor tour.
example.zh: 戶外導覽請帶一件外套。

example.en: The heater in my office stopped working this morning.
example.zh: 我辦公室的暖氣機今天早上壞了。

example.en: A cool breeze came through the open window.
example.zh: 一陣涼風從開著的窗戶吹進來。

derived.link: 最基礎的字。chilly = chill + -y，變成形容詞，像 sun → sunny、rain → rainy

example.en: Bring a sweater because the evenings are chilly here.
example.zh: 請帶一件毛衣，因為這裡的傍晚很涼。

senses.distinguish: 後面接 reply、reception、look 這類字時，指態度冷淡，不是天氣冷。

example.en: The client gave us a chilly reply to our offer.
example.zh: 客戶對我們的提案回覆得很冷淡。

extra_vocab.en: a person who works in a shop or office and helps customers or does paperwork
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於零售、飯店、銀行與辦公室情境，例如 sales clerk、desk clerk、office clerk。

example.en: Three clerks handle customer questions at the information counter.
example.zh: 三位店員在服務台處理顧客的問題。

example.en: The sales clerk helped me find a larger size.
example.zh: 銷售店員幫我找到比較大的尺寸。

example.en: The hotel desk clerk gave us two room keys.
example.zh: 飯店櫃檯人員給了我們兩把房間鑰匙。

example.en: We are hiring an office clerk to answer phones.
example.zh: 我們正在僱用一名辦公室職員來接電話。

examples.en: The clerk wrapped the gift and handed me the receipt.
examples.zh: 店員包好禮物，並把收據遞給我。

examples.en: Please ask the clerk at the front desk for an extra towel.
examples.zh: 請向櫃檯人員多要一條毛巾。

examples.en: She works as a clerk at the city office.
examples.zh: 她在市政府辦公室擔任職員。

similar.diff: cashier 專指收銀、收錢的人；clerk 範圍更廣，包含銷售與文書工作。

example.en: The cashier counted the money twice before closing.
example.zh: 收銀員在打烊前把錢數了兩次。

similar.diff: assistant 是協助主管或同事的助理；clerk 偏重處理櫃檯與文書事務。

example.en: The assistant booked the meeting room for Friday.
example.zh: 助理訂了星期五的會議室。

example.en: The receptionist greeted each visitor with a smile.
example.zh: 櫃檯人員微笑迎接每位訪客。

example.en: The staff meets every Monday to plan the week.
example.zh: 員工每星期一開會規劃一週工作。

example.en: Each employee must sign the new safety rules.
example.zh: 每位員工都必須簽署新的安全規定。

example.en: Please ask your supervisor to approve the request.
example.zh: 請請你的主管核准這項申請。

derived.link: clerk 的 -k 換成 -ical，變成形容詞「文書的」，像 music → musical

senses.en: a person who sells things to customers in a shop

example.en: The store clerk showed me three different laptops.
example.zh: 店員給我看了三台不同的筆電。

senses.en: a person who does office work such as filing and records
senses.distinguish: 句中有 office、accounting、files 等字時，通常指辦公室裡的文書人員。

example.en: A clerk in the accounting office sorts the invoices.
example.zh: 會計室的一位職員負責整理發票。

extra_vocab.en: the number of copies sold, or the movement of things from place to place
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於媒體（報紙雜誌的發行量）、金融（流通中的貨幣）與辦公環境（空氣流通）情境。

example.en: Circulation figures rose after the magazine changed its cover.
example.zh: 雜誌換封面後，發行量數字上升了。

example.en: The newspaper has a daily circulation of fifty thousand copies.
example.zh: 這份報紙每日發行量為五萬份。

example.en: Many old coins are no longer in circulation.
example.zh: 許多舊硬幣已不再流通。

example.en: Good air circulation keeps the warehouse cool in summer.
example.zh: 良好的空氣流通讓倉庫夏天保持涼爽。

example.en: Regular walking at lunch can improve your blood circulation.
example.zh: 午餐時固定散步可以改善你的血液循環。

examples.en: The magazine's circulation grew by ten percent last year.
examples.zh: 這本雜誌的發行量去年成長了百分之十。

examples.en: The new report is now in circulation among all department heads.
examples.zh: 新報告現在正在各部門主管之間傳閱。

examples.en: Open the windows to improve circulation in the meeting room.
examples.zh: 打開窗戶以改善會議室的空氣流通。

confusable.diff: circular 當形容詞是「圓形的」，當名詞是「傳閱的通知、傳單」；circulation 是發行量或流通。
confusable.usage: circular 是形容詞或名詞，circulation 是名詞，意思不同，詞性也不同。

example.en: The company sent a circular to all employees on Monday.
example.zh: 公司星期一寄了一份傳閱通知給所有員工。

similar.diff: distribution 重點在把商品分送到各地；circulation 常指報章雜誌的發行量或東西的流通。

example.en: The distribution of the new catalog begins next week.
example.zh: 新目錄的發送從下星期開始。

similar.diff: readership 是讀者人數；circulation 是賣出或發出的份數。

example.en: The magazine has a large readership among young workers.
example.zh: 這本雜誌在年輕上班族之間有很多讀者。

example.en: The latest edition of the guide includes new maps.
example.zh: 指南的最新版本包含新的地圖。

example.en: Your subscription will end on the first of March.
example.zh: 你的訂閱將在三月一日到期。

example.en: The publisher plans to print more copies next month.
example.zh: 出版商計畫下個月多印一些。

derived.link: 最基礎的字，指「圓圈」。circulation 就是東西繞圈流動、到處流通
circulation 去掉 -ion 加 -e，變成動詞，像 educate → education
circle 的 -le 換成 -ular，變成形容詞「圓形的」，像 single → singular

senses.en: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold

example.en: Our weekly paper has a circulation of about ten thousand.
example.zh: 我們的週報發行量大約一萬份。

senses.en: the movement of money, news, or papers from person to person
senses.distinguish: 後面接 money、coins、documents 時，指東西在人與人之間流通。

example.en: The rumor was already in wide circulation by noon.
example.zh: 到中午時，這個謠言已經廣為流傳。

senses.en: the movement of air or blood around a space or body
senses.distinguish: 和 blood、air、room 等字一起出現時，指循環或流通。

example.en: A fan helps the circulation of air in the small office.
example.zh: 風扇有助於小辦公室的空氣流通。

extra_vocab.en: lasting for a long time or happening again and again
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於醫療保險、員工健康福利，也用在 chronic shortage、chronic problem 這類長期難解決的問題。

example.en: The insurance plan covers many chronic diseases.
example.zh: 這個保險方案涵蓋許多慢性疾病。

example.en: Long hours at a desk can lead to chronic back pain.
example.zh: 長時間坐在書桌前可能導致慢性背痛。

example.en: The hospital faces a chronic shortage of trained nurses.
example.zh: 這間醫院長期缺乏受過訓練的護理師。

example.en: Late deliveries are a chronic problem for this supplier.
example.zh: 延遲交貨是這家供應商長期存在的問題。

examples.en: Employees with chronic conditions can get extra health support.
examples.zh: 有慢性疾病的員工可以獲得額外的健康支援。

examples.en: The factory has a chronic delay in shipping orders.
examples.zh: 這間工廠長期有出貨延遲的問題。

examples.en: Chronic traffic jams make the daily commute very hard.
examples.zh: 長期的交通堵塞讓每天通勤非常辛苦。

confusable.diff: acute 是急性的，突然發生、很嚴重；chronic 是慢性的，持續很久。

example.en: He went to the hospital because of acute stomach pain.
example.zh: 他因為急性胃痛去了醫院。

confusable.diff: chronicle 是名詞，指「編年史、紀事」，拼法開頭和 chronic 很像。

example.en: The book is a chronicle of the company's early years.
example.zh: 這本書記錄了公司早期的歷史。

similar.diff: long-term 只強調時間長；chronic 常帶有難以改善、令人困擾的感覺。

example.en: The company needs a long-term solution to the staff shortage.
example.zh: 公司需要一個長期的方法來解決人手不足。

similar.diff: ongoing 是「持續進行中」，語氣中性；chronic 多指不好的長期狀況。

example.en: We are dealing with an ongoing problem in the system.
example.zh: 我們正在處理系統裡持續發生的問題。

example.en: A shortage of parts slowed production last month.
example.zh: 零件短缺讓上個月的生產變慢了。

example.en: Please see a doctor if the symptoms continue.
example.zh: 如果症狀持續，請去看醫生。

example.en: A persistent noise in the machine worried the engineers.
example.zh: 機器裡持續的噪音讓工程師們很擔心。

example.en: The patient's condition is getting better each day.
example.zh: 病人的狀況一天比一天好。

derived.link: chronic + -ally，形容詞變副詞，像 basic → basically

senses.en: describing an illness that lasts a long time

example.en: Chronic illness can make it hard to work full time.
example.zh: 慢性疾病可能讓人難以全職工作。

senses.en: describing a bad problem that never goes away
senses.distinguish: 後面接 shortage、delay、problem 時，指長期存在的問題，不是疾病。

example.en: The company has a chronic lack of skilled drivers.
example.zh: 這家公司長期缺乏有經驗的司機。
